note_add: Delaware charges a daily vehicle entrance fee March 1 to November 30 (2026: $5 inland and $10 beach parks for Delaware-registered vehicles, $10 and $20 for out-of-state ones; annual pass $50 resident, $100 non-resident), but campers do not pay it for the camping unit and one vehicle: the site comes with a pass for one vehicle, which does not cover the camping unit itself, so a motorhome towing a car pays nothing at the gate. Further vehicles go to overflow parking. A site holds one camping unit, one vehicle at the site, and four people before the $2 per person per night additional-camper fee. Non-residents pay 1.25 times the resident price, rounded up to the dollar. Rates vary by season and by weekday or weekend, park by park, so the entries carry their own weekend premiums. The $4 reservation transaction fee is per reservation. Delaware has no sales tax, and its 8% lodging tax (30 Del. C. 6102) is defined on rooms in a hotel, motel or tourist home, which does not name campsites.

note_add: Every campground reservation, walk-ins and in-person bookings included, pays a $5 transaction fee on top of the park use fee, and a change costs $5. Family campsites are $20 a night for NJ residents and $25 for non-residents, the same every night (the fee schedule in N.J.A.C. 7:2-17.2 has no weekend, holiday or per-person charge). Two vehicles of any type may park at a site at no charge; more park in designated lots at $5 a night each. Pets $5 a night. At most six people a site unless they are all one family. No sales tax or occupancy fee on campsites (Tax Topic Bulletin S&U-13). Summer parking fees ($5-20 a vehicle a day, Memorial Day to Labor Day, N.J.A.C. 7:2-17.1) are not stated to apply to campers.
